content.rendered:
Who I am

I’m Daniel Nowak. I fix how revenue and operations actually run, and then apply AI where it compounds.

I didn’t arrive at AI from engineering. I arrived from operations: eighteen years of them, thirteen spent running restaurants, conference floors and hotel F&B departments in Poland and Ireland. In that world a broken process isn’t a slide in a deck. It’s a room full of people waiting for their food, and you find out within the hour.

That taught me the thing I still sell today: the bottleneck is almost never the tool. It’s the handoff.

I do that work independently through DNA4Digital, and as Associate Partner at Yameo (a Dutch-Polish enterprise software house) when a client needs the system built as well as designed.

My story How I work What I do
#1
revenue team in EMEA, Google Customer Solutions
5×
increase in funnel engagement
30%
cut in ticket handling time
+20–40%
faster processes once the work is organised

Why I do this

I moved into tech in 2021, and I kept noticing the same thing from the inside that I’d seen from the kitchen pass: companies buying tools to solve problems that were never tool problems. Technology without business context doesn’t fix anything. It just relocates the mess and makes it faster. So I work the other way round: process first, then automation, then AI.

My story. Thirteen years in hospitality operations: opening a café and bakery in Donegal National Park, running four F&B outlets and 600 covers a day at the Royal Marine, rebuilding a hotel restaurant into a takeaway business in the first weeks of COVID with nothing but Facebook, Google Ads and a redrawn menu. Along the way I learned SOPs, forecasting, margin control, and what happens to a team when the process is unclear.

In 2021 I joined TTEC as a Google Ads account manager. Promoted to POD Lead in four months, then to Team Leader running Google Customer Solutions for Poland and CZ/SK, as a TTEC vendor partner. That team finished #1 for revenue in EMEA, and I took the Platinum Club award for best manager in the region. I also held a 5/5 employee satisfaction score for four straight quarters. Nobody left, and that protected the margin.

Then I went technical. At Sensay, an AI SaaS company, I stopped selling and started building: migrating legacy systems into HubSpot, enriching the data with Breeze Intelligence, engineering automated sequences in n8n and Zapier, and assembling Looker Studio dashboards that merged CRM, product and website analytics. Funnel engagement went up fivefold.

At SpotOn I ran client operations for a restaurant-tech platform, and the same pattern held: audit the workflows, automate the right ones, cut ticket handling time by 30%, and rebuild the SOPs so the answers live somewhere other than in people’s heads. Which, given where I started, felt like the circle closing.

I’m now Associate Partner at Yameo, a Dutch–Polish software house that has been building enterprise systems for banking, insurance and healthcare since 2006. That partnership matters for one practical reason: when the work I’ve mapped needs engineers to build it, I have a team behind me that ships on fixed price, fixed date and a signed SLA. Most independent consultants have to hand you a plan and wish you luck.

Why work with me

No “AI magic,” and no pretending the tool is the answer. You get a transparent plan, fast pilots, and effects you can measure: time back, cleaner data, revenue that moves. You also get me, not a pitch team followed by a delivery team you’ve never met. I’m a Lean Six Sigma Black Belt with a Machine Learning with Python certification, which is a strange combination and exactly the point.

What I stand for

Simplicity: if a process can’t be explained in one page, it won’t be followed.
Accountability: I name the number, the baseline and the timeframe. Every time.
Partnership: I only teach what I’ve run myself, in a live business, with consequences.

The arc

Hospitality taught me operations. Google taught me scale. Sensay taught me to build the thing instead of just specifying it. Yameo means I can now build the ones that are too big for one person.

How I work

From diagnosis to rollout and scale, without chaos and without burning out your team.

1. Audit & process map

I map how work actually moves, not how the org chart says it does. Bottlenecks, handoffs, duplicated fields, the workarounds everyone has quietly built. You get the friction ranked by what it costs you.

More about audits →

2. Pilot & training

We test on live examples with your data, I train the people who’ll run it, and we pick tools that fit the process rather than the other way round.

More about training →

3. Implementation & scale

Standards, SOPs, KPIs and dashboards, so the improvement survives after I’ve gone.

More about consulting →

Three things I’m actually good at

Eighteen years of operations across hospitality, BPO and SaaS, applied to marketing, sales, customer operations and back-office.

Go-to-market & RevOps

Funnel and pipeline design, qualification rules, handoffs, CRM architecture and reporting. I’ve built intent-driven prospecting off ICP and buyer-persona mapping, run A/B tests across outbound cadences that lifted engagement 18%, and migrated a legacy stack into a unified HubSpot instance that C-level could actually read. Tools: HubSpot, Salesforce, Breeze Intelligence, Looker Studio.

Process architecture & operations

Mapping, standardisation, ownership, SOPs, KPIs and quality control. This is the Lean Six Sigma half: unglamorous, and the half that decides whether anything else works. Most “AI problems” turn out to be undocumented processes wearing a costume.

AI enablement & automation

Low-code architecture in n8n and Zapier, AI-enhanced training programmes, internal troubleshooting chatbots, e-commerce sales assistants and concierge bots. Plus the governance nobody wants to write: internal SOPs, GDPR data-sharing agreements, and a framework that keeps your analytics integrations defensible.

Where this experience comes from

Eighteen years of operations across hospitality, BPO and SaaS, in Poland, Ireland and across EMEA.

Yameo, Associate Partner

Enterprise software delivery for banking, insurance, healthcare and the public sector.

Google Customer Solutions

Led the PL and CZ/SK team as a TTEC vendor partner. #1 revenue team in EMEA; Platinum Club, Best Manager, Q3 2024.

TTEC, Team Leader

EMEA Business Development. Enterprise BPO solutioning and C-level negotiation.

Sensay, Senior Technical BDM

RevOps architecture and AI product deployment.

SpotOn, Client Operations Manager

Workflow automation and operational enablement.

Balkans Crypto, Sales Director

Commercial strategy for a 2,000-attendee Web3 conference; Tier-1 exchange and L1/L2 partnerships.

Credentials: Lean Six Sigma Black Belt · Machine Learning with Python (V2) · Web Development · BA Economics (Wyższa Szkoła Finansów i Informatyki, 2026)

Daniel Nowak is an Associate Partner at Yameo B.V. Where a client engagement leads to software delivery by Yameo, I have a commercial interest in that work. I’ll tell you that in the first conversation, not the fifth.

Ready to give technology some meaning?

Book a free 30-minute call. I’ll tell you where I’d start, and whether the first move is an audit, a pilot, or simply writing down how the work is supposed to happen.

Book a consultation See services
Transparent plan Practical tools Measurable results

content.rendered:
Practical AI implementation, with a return you can see

I put AI where it genuinely pays off. Through training, audits and advisory, I help companies work faster, cleaner and smarter. My bias is towards practical implementation and results you notice immediately, no theorising, no chaos, concrete business value.

Book a free consultation GTM & processes
Training Audits / AI Readiness
Consulting & implementation
Speed and precision
in the areas that matter strategically

Go-to-market and the processes underneath it

This is where I do my best work, and where most AI spending goes to die. Companies point AI at the visible layer: writing the emails, summarising the calls, generating the content. Underneath, the pipeline stages mean different things to different people, leads sit in a gap between marketing and sales for four days, the CRM has three fields for the same thing, and nobody has written down what “qualified” means.

Automating that doesn’t fix it. It scales it. So I work both layers, in order: make the revenue process legible, then apply AI where it compounds.

Revenue process mapping

The full journey from first touch to closed and renewed. Stage definitions, exit criteria, owners, and every handoff where things currently fall over.

Funnel & pipeline hygiene

Qualification rules that hold, forecast inputs you can trust, CRM fields people actually fill in because they’re worth filling in.

GTM automation

Research, enrichment, routing, follow-up, call notes and reporting. Applied to a process that works, so the gains stick.

Enablement for revenue teams

SDRs, AEs, marketing and CS trained on the workflows for their role, using your data and your deals. Not a generic prompt library.

What you get: a mapped GTM process, a list of the friction points ranked by cost, and a 90-day plan splitting them into “fix the process” and “automate it.”

Book a consultation

Two ways this ends

Most engagements start the same way: an audit, a process map, a ranked list of what’s costing you money. Where they go next depends on what the answer turns out to be.

If the fix is process and configuration, I do it. Automations, CRM architecture, SOPs, dashboards, and training your team so it runs without me. Weeks, not quarters.

If the fix needs software built, I bring in Yameo, a Dutch–Polish software house that has been delivering enterprise systems for banking, insurance and healthcare since 2006. Fixed price, fixed date, signed SLA. I’m an Associate Partner there, and I stay on the engagement as the person who owns whether it actually solves your problem.

You’re never handed off to strangers, and you’re never sold a build you didn’t need.

I do this myself (DNA4Digital)

GTM and revenue process design
Process mapping, SOPs, KPIs
AI readiness audits and roadmaps
Low-code automation (n8n, Zapier, HubSpot)
Training and enablement
Dashboards and reporting (Looker Studio)

I bring in the team (via Yameo)

Custom software and platform builds
System integrations and migrations at scale
Regulated-industry work needing compliance sign-off
Anything needing an engineering team for months
Fixed-price, fixed-date, SLA-backed delivery
Long-term embedded development partnership

The rule of thumb: if it can be done with configuration, I do it. If it needs code, engineers and a signed SLA, Yameo builds it and I stay on as the person who owns the outcome.

Training and workshops

I build practical programmes around the roles and processes that exist in your company. We work on your real data and your real tasks, so people can use AI in their actual job the same week. Knowledge plus practice, measurable and fast.

Marketing & sales

Funnels, content, research, analytics, CRM support: a set of ready-to-run workflows.

Operations & administration

Document standardisation, order in procedures, quality control and automation.

HR & knowledge

Onboarding, knowledge repositories, policies and SOPs. AI in the service of people.

Audits

I analyse your processes and your data to find where AI will pay back first. You get a practical implementation plan that lets you act strategically and hit measurable results, without chaos and without unnecessary complexity.


See the audit offer

Assessment progress0% → 100%
AI Readiness Audit
Initial score + action plan

After the workshop you leave with priorities, a process map and tool recommendations.

Book a consultation

Consulting

I implement AI end to end, from quick wins to durable working standards. Automations, AI assistants, knowledge repositories and SOPs, so the technology genuinely supports the business. Practical and strategic in equal measure, so every change earns its keep and every implementation fits how your organisation actually operates.

Quick wins

ROI mapping and the first automations that give your team its time back.

Assistants & automation

Prompt design, policies and integrations. Stable, auditable workflows.

Knowledge repos & SOPs

Standardised documents, policies and checklists: knowledge that’s current and easy to find.

Book a free consultation Start with training

Selected work

These are results from roles I’ve held as an employee, not consulting engagements delivered under DNA4Digital. I’m labelling each one with the company and my role, so the context is never in question.

Book a free consultation See my full track record
#1
revenue team in EMEA, Google Customer Solutions
5×
increase in funnel engagement (Sensay)
30%
cut in ticket handling time (SpotOn)

Migrated a legacy CRM into a unified HubSpot instance, and grew funnel engagement fivefold

Context: As Senior Technical Business Development Manager at Sensay, an AI SaaS company.

The problem: Data lived across a legacy CRM and disconnected tools, with no single source of truth for revenue data. Reporting to leadership meant manual reconciliation rather than a number anyone could just look up.

What I did: Migrated the legacy stack into a single HubSpot instance, enriched contact and account data with Breeze Intelligence, and engineered automated sequences in n8n and Zapier to keep the data current without manual entry. Then built Looker Studio dashboards merging CRM, product and website analytics into one view.

The result: Funnel engagement increased fivefold.

What I’d tell you if you’re facing this: A CRM migration that doesn’t start with agreeing what your key terms mean (qualified, engaged, active) just moves the mess into a nicer-looking tool. Fix the definitions before you fix the system.

Cut ticket handling time by 30% by rebuilding the workflow, not just automating it

Context: As Client Operations Manager at SpotOn, a restaurant-tech platform, owning the support and operations workflow for the client base.

The problem: Ticket handling was inconsistent. The right answer to a common issue depended on which team member picked it up, because the knowledge lived in people’s heads rather than in a documented process.

What I did: Audited the existing workflow end to end, rebuilt the SOPs so the correct answer was documented and easy to find, and automated the repetitive parts of the workflow around that new standard.

The result: Ticket handling time dropped by 30%.

What I’d tell you if you’re facing this: Automating a broken process just makes the mess move faster. Document the correct process first. The automation almost writes itself once that part is done.

Built the automation layer nobody had to be told to use

Context: Also at Sensay, alongside the CRM migration, building the automation and reporting layer underneath the sales and marketing workflow.

The problem: Reporting tools already existed, but the team rarely opened them, because the numbers didn’t match what people saw in the systems they actually used day to day.

What I did: Built the n8n and Zapier automations around the workflows the team already used, rather than asking them to adopt a new tool, and built the dashboards on top of the same data everyone already trusted, merging CRM, product and website analytics into one Looker Studio view.

The result: The dashboards became the thing leadership actually opened, because the numbers finally matched what the team saw on the ground.

What I’d tell you if you’re facing this: Adoption is the metric everyone skips when reporting on an automation project. If nobody opens the dashboard, the automation didn’t work, no matter how clever it is.

Want results like these?

Book a free 30-minute call and we’ll work out whether the first move is an audit, a pilot, or simply writing down how the work is supposed to happen.

DNA 4DIGITAL
I’m Daniel Nowak. AI consulting built around:

The world is speeding up, and technology keeps opening new doors. AI, digital tools and automation are genuinely changing how we work and how we spend our time. But it’s easy to lose control in all of it: instead of technology working for you, you end up working for it.

That’s why I focus on go-to-market and the processes underneath it, the part most AI projects skip. Marketing, sales, customer operations: the places where a broken handoff costs more than any tool can save. I fix the process first, then apply AI to it. In that order, it works.

I bring 18 years of hospitality, revenue-operations and AI experience to the table, because tools change every quarter. Judgement doesn’t.

SEE MY TRACK RECORD

0×

0%

See the return tomorrow

Skills that hold up in practice

I combine human experience with modern tools,
because only a human can give technology, and an AI transformation, real meaning.

I give teams the knowledge and tools to:

  • take back control of their time
    and how work is organised
  • clean up internal processes
    and procedures
  • adopt AI and new technology
    in a practical, non-theoretical way
  • work effectively, without chaos
    and without the stress

GTM design & optimisation

Your funnel, your handoffs, your qualification rules, your CRM. I map how revenue actually moves through the company. Then I remove the friction before adding a single tool.

More →

Process architecture

Mapping, standardisation, ownership and KPIs. Most “AI problems” turn out to be undocumented processes wearing a costume. I make the work legible first.

More →

Strategic audits

I don’t just train. I analyse and advise. Audits and consulting to tighten processes, introduce procedures and build systems that actually get used.

More →

Expert training

I choose the tools and design AI solutions that fit your processes, from concept and PoC to a stable rollout and a team that knows how to run it.

More →

Professional consulting

I diagnose your processes, your data and your organisation’s readiness for AI, then flag the risks and the automation potential. You get priorities, quick wins and a 90-day action map.

More →

A holistic view

I translate business goals into concrete initiatives: operating model, KPIs, governance and change roadmaps, working alongside your leadership and your teams.

More →

Is your company ready for AI?

Eight questions, two minutes. You’ll find out where your organisation actually sits on the AI curve, and get my recommendations for what to do next.

  • Register on our website,
  • Subscribe to our newsletters,
  • Participate in promotional activities,
  • Interact with our marketing efforts.

This data may include your name, email address, phone number, profession, and demographic information such as age and location.

Usage Data: We automatically collect data generated by your use of our services, such as your IP address, browser type, and browsing history.

Purpose of Processing: We process your personal data to:

  • Provide and maintain our services,
  • Personalize your website experience,
  • Communicate with you about products and services that may be of interest,
  • Conduct analytics and market research,
  • Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements.

Lawful Basis: We process personal data based on:

  • Your consent,
  • The necessity to fulfill a contract with you,
  • Our legitimate business interests,
  • Legal obligations.

2. Consent

When you provide us with personal data to complete a transaction, verify your credit card, or place an order, we imply that you consent to our collecting it and using it for that specific reason only.

If we ask for your personal data for a secondary reason, like marketing, we will either ask you directly for your expressed consent or provide you with an opportunity to say no.

3. Withdrawal of Consent

If after you opt-in, you change your mind, you may withdraw your consent for us to contact you, for the continued collection, use, or disclosure of your information, at any time, by contacting us at [Insert Email] or mailing us at [Insert Address].

4. Disclosure of Data

We may disclose your personal data if we are required by law to do so or if you violate our Terms of Service.

5. Data Security

We take all reasonable steps to ensure that your data is treated securely and in accordance with this Privacy Policy. No method of transmission over the Internet or method of electronic storage is 100% secure, but we follow all GDPR requirements and implement additional generally accepted industry standards.

6. Data Retention

We will retain your personal data only for as long as is necessary for the purposes set out in this Privacy Policy. We will retain and use your data to the extent necessary to comply with our legal obligations, resolve disputes, and enforce our policies.

7. Rights Under GDPR

Under GDPR, you have various rights including:

  • The right to access, update or to delete the information we have on you.
  • The right of rectification.
  • The right to object.
  • The right of restriction.
  • The right to data portability.
  • The right to withdraw consent.

Please contact us if you wish to exercise any of these rights.

8. Third-Party Services

We may use third-party service providers to assist us in operating our website and conducting our business. These third-party services may include payment processors, email service providers, and marketing platforms. While we strive to work with reputable providers, we encourage you to review their privacy policies as we do not control their practices and are not responsible for their content or actions.

9. International Data Transfers

If you are located in the European Economic Area (EEA), please note that any information we collect from you may be transferred to and processed in countries outside of the EEA, which may not have the same level of data protection as your home country. When we do so, we ensure that there are adequate safeguards in place to protect your personal data in accordance with GDPR requirements.

10. Cookies and Tracking Technologies

Our website uses cookies and similar tracking technologies to enhance user experience and analyze site usage. Cookies are small files that are stored on your device and can be retrieved by our servers. You can control the use of cookies at the individual browser level, but if you choose to disable cookies, it may limit your ability to use certain features or functions of our website.

We use the following types of cookies:

  • Essential Cookies: Required for the operation of our website.
  • Analytical/Performance Cookies: Help us understand how visitors interact with our website.
  • Marketing Cookies: Used to deliver advertisements relevant to you and your interests.

By using our website, you consent to our use of cookies in accordance with this Privacy Policy.

11. Changes to This Privacy Policy

We may update our Privacy Policy from time to time. We will notify you of any changes by posting the new Privacy Policy on this page and updating the effective date at the top of the policy. We encourage you to review this Privacy Policy periodically for any updates.

12. Contact Us

If you have any questions or concerns regarding this Privacy Policy or our data practices, please contact us at:

Email: dn@dna4digital.com

13. Complaints

If you believe that we have not complied with your data protection rights, you have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority in your country of residence.
